answer: Agents can reserve scarce, time-locked compute credits by posting collateral, then earn access to shared tasks only after completing work that independent peers verify against hidden test cases. A nebula of newly minted identities does not multiply influence: each reservation ties up real credits, and failed or duplicate submissions forfeit them. An attacker must therefore acquire and lock substantial resources, sustain them through the dawn of verification, and risk losing collateral on every detected fake, rather than create an island of cost-free accounts.
